persistence.scope: Public UI in Chromium with an in-memory native IPC/filesystem model. This verifies client ownership and routing, not actual OS I/O, WKWebView, permissions or atomic replacement.

actualMacOSWebView.scope: Actual bundled native UI, IPC and temporary filesystem recovery; macOS runs WKWebView. Does not exercise OS file picker dialogs, manual visual acceptance, physical Android or another host platform.

independentNativeReview.scope: Independent synthetic filesystem checks. No actual user appData/recovery contents were accessed.

limits: Debug standalone module process; excludes IPC copies, WebView, JS document/history, worker/codec memory.
65 and 300 MiB sequential manual-save plus recovery-write/read in one process; allocator retention affects peak.
Input byte buffer dropped before recovery read. Every recovered payload byte verified.
Wall times are a single run, not p50/p95/p99 and not a controlled old/new performance comparison.

qtInteroperability.result: Actual temporary Qt process live exclusive lock blocks read-only shared guard; own child SIGKILL leaves unchanged stale lock that permits guarded read; Qt stale reclaim blocked while shared guard is held; reclaim succeeds after release.
qtInteroperability.limits: macOS Qt6.12 only. Full pathname lifecycle is not equivalent to same-inode flock exclusion.

remainingLimits: Windows runtime, filesystem share/reparse and ACL behavior not executed here. Windows cross-target typecheck is assigned architect.

Final check then rename is best-effort detection of uncooperative external writers, not portable filesystem compare-and-swap.
1 GiB quota counts committed recovery payloads. Envelope headers, temporary save/recovery stages and crash-orphan stages require additional disk space.
Directory fsync failure after atomic rename is logged; already committed file remains successful but power-loss durability is not proven.

actualFinalNativeCLI.scope: Actual final debug binary --io-smoke, branch before Tauri setup; exclusively fresh temporary root; 65 and300 MiB sequential recovery write/read. No WebView or actual user appData.
